description:
calendar.rs:76-77, event.rs:85-86, event.rs:128-129, event_notification.rs:119-120, participant_identity.rs:63-64, event_copy.rs:19 all accept `create: Option<serde_json::Value>`, `update: Option<serde_json::Value>`, `filter: Option<serde_json::Value>`, `sort: Option<serde_json::Value>`.

This is the JSON-blob anti-pattern. The whole point of jmap-calendars-types is to provide typed Calendar, CalendarEvent, etc. — but the client API throws that away and accepts any JSON shape, defers all validation to the server, and gives no compile-time feedback to the caller.

The PLAN.md (lines 122, 172, 188-202) specifies typed builders: `SetRequest<Calendar>`, `CalendarEventQueryRequest`, `CalendarComparator`, `CalendarEventFilterCondition`. None of these were implemented.

Consequence today: caller writes
```
sc.calendar_event_set(Some(json!({"newEv": {"calendarIds": ...}})), None, None).await?;
```
with a typo `calendaIds` and the compiler is silent. Server returns invalidArguments.

Idiomatic fix is exactly what PLAN.md described. This is an API-design Section 1 issue: post-1.0 the signature is locked. Lock the right one. (cross-crate: jmap-mail-client has the same shape.)

Note: switching to typed builders likely changes the public API of `calendar_set`, `calendar_event_set`, `participant_identity_set`, `calendar_event_copy`, `calendar_event_query`, `calendar_event_notification_query` simultaneously. Coordinate the change.
title: create/update/filter/sort take Option<serde_json::Value> — stringly-typed JMAP API
